factual_summaries: Microsoft Incident Response described an MCP tool-description poisoning pattern where changed tool metadata can steer an acting agent to retrieve sensitive records and send them through an approved tool call. The guidance recommends publisher allowlists, tool-metadata review, prompt/content inspection, DLP on tool parameters, human approval for high-impact actions, agent identities, telemetry correlation, and least-agency controls.

TechRadar reported SentinelOne analysis of macOS.Gaslight, malware that embeds fake Markdown-like system messages intended to mislead LLM-assisted malware triage. The report says the malware also includes backdoor and infostealer behavior, making untrusted binary contents both an instruction-injection risk and a sensitive-data/security-analysis risk.

LightOn compared agent runs over document corpora with direct file reading versus search-backed retrieval. It reported that dedicated search reduced token use while preserving or improving judged answer quality, especially as the corpus grew and raw reading hit context limits.

LightOn described faceted search for AI retrieval, arguing that typed document metadata and pre-filtering can scope the corpus before semantic or hybrid search runs, reducing noise before content reaches the model context.
